description_full: Georgia Banking Company, Inc. engages in banking business to individual, business, and commercial customers in Atlanta, Georgia. It provides accounts, savings, certificate of deposits, loan payments, mortgage lending, and digital and private banking services to individuals. The company also offers business accounts, savings, digital banking, online loan payment, and treasury solutions to businesses. In addition, it provides construction loans, real estate lending, payments, digital banking, online payments, and other services. The company was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.

financial_summary: Georgia Banking Company, Inc. is a small-cap financial services business with a $353M market cap on $113M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +43% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

The business throws off $23M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.08× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 0.7% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 24% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
